In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. Jeveration builds on a frozen vision-language model, repurposing its visual-semantic knowledge for holistic image generation. The key challenge is to maintain global consistency. vyzkum.nazev: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
vyzkum.souhrn: Agent evolution follows a simple loop: a proposer writes candidate artifacts (prompts, skills, memories) and selection accepts those that score higher. This loop has shown promise, yet practitioners face a puzzle: methods trade wins across papers, and evolution often fails to bootstrap on certain tasks. We trace this puzzle to the Resolution Hypothesis: agent evolution stalls not because methods fail to propose better artifacts, but because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify them.…

We construct ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K for two-stage training. vyzkum.souhrn: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. Existing datasets also cover a limited range of games, often without explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. vyzkum.souhrn: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. vyzkum.souhrn: Multimodal tabular learning involves classification and regression on tables combining structured numerical and categorical features with unstructured text and images. These unstructured fields are commonly represented by pretrained encoder embeddings reduced with principal component analysis (PCA). For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors.
